ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A, B, C$ lie on circle $\odot O$, and $\angle ACB = 40^\circ$. What is the degree measure of arc $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AOB$ and $\angle ACB$ both subtend $\overset{\frown}{AB}$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOB=2\angle ACB=2\times 40^\circ=80^\circ$,\\
thus, the measure of arc $AB$ is $\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, points A, B, and C are all on the circumference, and O is marked inside the circle; from C to A and B, chords CA and CB are connected respectively, so angle ∠ACB is formed at point C. The problem statement gives ∠ACB = 40°, and asks for the measure of arc AB. Reasoning: ∠ACB is an inscribed angle formed by chords CA and CB, and what it intercepts is arc AB not containing C. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of an inscribed angle equals half the measure of its intercepted arc, therefore the measure of arc AB = 2 × ∠ACB = 2 × 40° = 80°.
